transcript:
16:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan Lee): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
16:01 Speaker 2 (Liam): Liam here from Brightlane procurement.
16:01 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha Khan): Aisha on the call from security.
16:01 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Ravi from platform.
16:01 Speaker 5 (Sofia): Sofia, legal counsel.
16:01 Speaker 6 (Ben): Ben, finance.
16:02 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great, quick agenda. We want to cover MSA / DPA items specific to marketplace distribution, billing and invoice flows for marketplace-sourced adopters, and then Maya will run through KMS preflight and options for key custody. We'll leave Q&A and next steps last.
16:03 Speaker 2 (Liam): Sounds good, high level we need to understand who owns encryption keys for data processed via the marketplace, and how billing will show up — does it come from Redwood or from Brightlane marketplace partner ledger, that sort of thing.
16:03 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): Also need assurance on audit logs, retention and how long the KV cache or cached prompts persist. We have tight PHI controls, so DPA scoping is critical.
16:04 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Totally — we can support a couple patterns: 1) Redwood manages keys (our KMS) with customer-managed envelopes (we can bring your KMS via external wrapping), 2) Customer-managed keys via BYOK where the key never leaves your KMS/HSM and we perform envelope encryption, or 3) a hybrid for marketplace where keys are rotated at the tenant level. Maya, quick overview?
16:05 Speaker 7 (Maya Patel): Yeah so on the SE side, for marketplace we usually recommend customer-managed wrapping for regulated customers. Practically that means Brightlane supplies an external KMS key (AWS KMS, CloudHSM, or equivalent) and we store a wrapped key in our vault. We can do either REST-based key calls or configure a VPC peered KMS proxy. There are tradeoffs — slightly higher latency on token generation but better isolation.
16:06 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): When you say 'we store a wrapped key' — is that a copy we could audit? We need to know rotation cadence and proof key material isn't exportable.
16:06 Speaker 7 (Maya): The wrapped key is not the raw key material; it's an encrypted blob that requires the customer's KMS to unwrap. We can provide rotation logs and attestations, and we include decryption attempts in audit trails. The raw key remains in your KMS.
16:07 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Practically, for staging we want a sample YAML or helm chart to test integration — network egress, ports, and expected ephemeral credentials.
16:08 Speaker 7 (Maya): Absolutely, I'll share a KMS preflight checklist including sample YAML, expected permissions, and a staging runbook.
16:09 Speaker 5 (Sofia): From a legal MSA/DPA perspective, a few items popped up in our preliminary review. One, limitation of liability in marketplace transactions; two, indemnities tied to data misuse; three, clarity around subprocessors when Brightlane customers connect via the marketplace.
16:10 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Understood. On subprocessors we maintain a registry and can add marketplace distribution as a subprocess category — we'll include marketplace partners in the subprocessor list and commit to 30 days notice for additions.
16:10 Speaker 5 (Sofia): That's good. For the DPA, we also need data residency guarantees for EU data and confirm any tokenization/pseudonymization controls.
16:11 Speaker 7 (Maya): We support region pinning; for the marketplace we can route EU workloads to our eu-central pair and ensure no token leaves. There are minimal caveats for cross-region fallbacks but those are configurable.
16:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): On billing — Ben can speak to finance, but our procurement wants predictability. Do Redwood marketplace charges flow through Redwood invoices, or do they show up as a separate marketplace line item billed by Brightlane? How does tax and VAT get handled?
16:12 Speaker 8 (Ben): Right now Finance wants to avoid surprise charges that look like passthroughs. We need example invoice format and a sample of net vs gross billing when marketplace margins apply.
16:13 Speaker 1 (Jordan): For marketplace sales we have two common models: you can have Redwood invoice Brightlane directly for usage (hosted marketplace model) or we support a marketplace passthrough where the marketplace aggregates billing and remits to Redwood — that complicates tax handling but is doable. I'll include two sample invoice flows: Redwood-direct and marketplace-passthrough with VAT breakdowns.
16:14 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Also, how are chargebacks handled if customer usage is contested? We need a dispute window and credit policy spelled out.
16:14 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We have an SLA remediation table in the MSA, standard 99.9% latency/uptime targets with tiered credits. For contested usage we have a 30-day dispute window and can coordinate an audit trace. We can expand dispute handling for marketplace sales.
16:15 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): Regarding SLA, what about PII leaks or infosec incidents? SOC 2 + incident response timelines?
16:15 Speaker 7 (Maya): We provide SOC 2 Type II reports; for major incidents we commit to notify within 72 hours and provide a post-incident report. We can add a special clause for PHI sensitivity with accelerated notification if needed.
16:16 Speaker 5 (Sofia): For the MSA redlines, I'd prefer to see a marketplace addendum that scopes responsibilities — less risky than reworking the main MSA. Can Redwood draft a concise marketplace addendum?
16:16 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Yes we can. We'll propose a marketplace addendum that defines distribution roles, revenue flow, subprocessor specifics, and KMS patterns.
16:17 Speaker 6 (Ben): One finance question: If Brightlane sells Redwood-based features through our marketplace to third parties, is there a revenue share and how is it reported? We need clarity on gross vs net revenue recognition.
16:17 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Revenue share can be handled via the partner program. For the pilot we can keep it simple — usage-based fees to Redwood and your marketplace applies its listing fee. We'll include a sample revenue share table in the pricing schedule.
16:18 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Back to tech — can we run benchmarks for latency impact of BYOK vs Redwood KMS in staging? Our app requires sub-100ms token latency for short prompts.
16:18 Speaker 7 (Maya): Yes, we'll instrument benchmarks. BYOK adds ~10-30ms per session bootstrap typically, but token generation path remains unchanged after initial handshake. For high-QPS workloads we recommend an ephemeral wrapping key to avoid per-request KMS calls. We'll provide perf numbers from similar customers.
16:20 Speaker 9 (Diego Ramos): Also noting caching behavior — KV cache retention defaults can impact prompt leakage risk; we can configure aggressive TTLs per tenant for marketplace listings.
16:21 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): Can you confirm log retention and redaction? We need to ensure logs that contain PII are not retained beyond 90 days unless audited.
16:21 Speaker 7 (Maya): Default logs 180 days, but we can set tenant overrides down to 30 days. We'll surface redaction controls in the console and produce audit logs as part of the SOC bundle.
16:22 Speaker 5 (Sofia): A legal nit — we want to see a clause where Brightlane or end-customers can request proof of deletion; how do we operationalize that?
16:22 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We can commit to deletion workflows and provide an admin API for data deletion requests with audit trails; we'll include this in the DPA.
16:24 Speaker 2 (Liam): Timelines — procurement needs final commercial terms in two weeks to hit our marketplace onboarding window. Is that feasible?
16:24 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We can aim for a 10 business day turnaround for a redline exchange. Jordan will send the redlined MSA/DPA and a marketplace addendum template by 2027-03-18.
16:25 Speaker 5 (Sofia): We'll try to get comments back by 2027-03-22. If legal needs a deeper conversation we'll flag it.
16:26 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): One more security question — for marketplace deployments, does Redwood isolate tenant model weights or is it multi-tenant at the inference layer? We need to understand attack surface.
16:27 Speaker 7 (Maya): Inference runtime is multi-tenant but with strict namespace isolation and per-tenant quotas, and model weights are read-only artifacts; we apply memory isolation and per-request tokenization namespaces. For ultra-sensitive workloads we recommend dedicated capacity or a private deployment.
16:28 Speaker 4 (Ravi): That raises a procurement question — will Brightlane require Dedicated for specific customers? We might have to carve out high-risk customers for dedicated deployments; how does that affect pricing?
16:29 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Dedicated pricing is a different SKU with reserved capacity; we'll include a delta pricing table so procurement can see the uplift.
16:30 Speaker 6 (Ben): On taxes and VAT, I'll need a sample invoice that shows how credits and refunds appear for marketplace passthroughs.
16:31 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll include two sample invoices and a simple reconciliation guide.
16:32 Speaker 7 (Maya): I'll attach the KMS preflight checklist to the follow-up email along with sample YAML and a runbook for staging.
16:33 Speaker 5 (Sofia): If you can also include an exhibit for breach notification timelines and liabilities for PHI that will accelerate our review.
16:33 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll draft an exhibit with accelerated notification for PHI + proposed liability carveouts for marketplace transactions.
16:34 Speaker 2 (Liam): Let's talk pilot acceptance criteria briefly — procurement wants a short checklist: security signoff, performance target, billing test, legal signoff.
16:35 Speaker 7 (Maya): Proposed pilot acceptance: 1) KMS preflight complete and keys validated, 2) latency within agreed bounds for 95th percentile, 3) successful end-to-end billing test with sample invoice, and 4) SOC 2 artifacts shared.
16:36 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Can we schedule a 2-hour technical pilot kickoff once KMS preflight results are in? Preferably next week.
16:36 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll be ready.
16:37 Speaker 6 (Ben): On financial approvals — once we receive pricing schedule we'll route to finance for signoff; expect 72 hrs to 5 business days depending on questions.
16:38 Speaker 9 (Diego): One small note — our marketplace has a certification badge for partners that pass security and performance checks. Completing pilot clears certification.
16:39 Speaker 3 (Dr. Aisha): That's helpful.
16:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Okay quick recap and owners. Jordan will send redlined MSA/DPA and marketplace addendum by 2027-03-18; Maya sends KMS checklist and staging YAML by 2027-03-17; Ravi provides VPC egress and TPS numbers by 2027-03-19; Sofia returns legal comments by 2027-03-22; schedule pilot kickoff after preflight.
16:41 Speaker 2 (Liam): Sounds good.
16:42 Speaker 5 (Sofia): Thanks all.
16:42 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
16:43 Speaker 2 (Liam): Bye.
